text:
elena: FYI hitting a weird perf regression on the paged FlashAttention variant when we enable interleaved KV packing for bf16 models. Token/sec drops ~30% for batch sizes 4 and 8 vs previous run.

matt: can you paste the perf output and which kernel was picked?

elena: kernel selected: flash_paged_v2_interleave (fallback path: flash_fused_small). repro script: 

```
# repro (docker image: redwood/infra-perf:latest)
python run_infer.py --model gpt-small-bf16 --batch 4 --seq 1024 --kv-layout interleaved --dtype bf16
# observed: token/s 1200 -> 850 after step ~120
```

elena: attached nvprof snippet (trimmed):

```
GPU kernel: flash_paged_v2_interleave  time: 2.12ms  occupancy: 68%  L2_reads: 1.2G  L2_writes: 0.9G  mem_stalls: high
GPU kernel: flash_fused_small         time: 1.75ms  occupancy: 52%  L2_reads: 900M  L2_writes: 600M
```

jia: interesting — flash_paged_v2_interleave should be faster on contig KV, but bf16 alignment might be causing bank conflicts on our paged allocator. any stride patterns in the KV offsets?

elena: yes, offsets look like: 0, 48, 96, 144... (48 bytes stride) for per-token KV; when we patch to 64-byte stride (pad to cacheline) perf recovers to ~1180 token/s.

sam: so alignment + dtype packing matters. did you try segregated (separate keys/vals layout) vs interleaved?

elena: yep — with segregated layout and 48-byte stride drop is only ~8%. interleaved suffers the most.

anil: could be warp-level bank aliasing on L2/SMEM. flash_paged_v2_interleave assumes 128-bit lanes; bf16 packing changes true stride per warp. Can you capture SASS counters for bank_conflicts?

elena: I ran cupti counter sample: `shared_bank_conflicts` spiked from 0.2k -> 48k during the slow kernel window.

matt: ok next steps: (1) add a quick padding heuristic in runtime when dtype==bf16 and layout==interleaved: align KV rows to 64 bytes; (2) fallback policy: prefer fused kernel when batch<8 for now; (3) add a perf test case to CI.

jia: +1. Also add a diagnostic metric: per-kernel bank conflict rate to the console so we can spot this earlier.

ops-bot: deploy-note: canary image `infra-perf:kv-align-ht` will be rolled to staging at 2024-08-14T09:30Z. Automatic rollback on token/s drop >15%.

sam: quick patch in runtime to pad to 64B gives immediate recovery on my machine. Patch: 
```
if dtype == 'bf16' and layout == 'interleaved':
    pad_bytes = (64 - (row_bytes % 64)) % 64
    row_stride += pad_bytes
```

anil: let's also add a microbench harness for stride sweep (32, 48, 64, 96) and log kernel selection decisions. We should also verify kernel heuristics: maybe they pick `flash_paged_v2_interleave` based on model dims only, not on runtime observed stride.

elena: opened PR with tests + docs: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infer/+/1234. includes perf numbers and CI jobs.

matt: nice. can someone file a short postmortem so we remember this pattern? kernel heuristics + dtype alignment -> bank conflicts -> big regression.

elena: filing now. TL;DR: interleaved layout + bf16 packing + 48-byte stride caused SMEM/L2 bank conflicts; quick fix = pad to 64B + metric + fallback policy.

jia: thanks — can we also run the same sweep on fused kernels? I want to see if fused has hidden regressions for larger batches.

elena: will run fused vs paged sweep tomorrow and post numbers here. :eyes:
